root_cause.text: The thermal core reused and reinitialized the `tz->poll_queue` delayed work from both `thermal_zone_pm_complete()` and `thermal_zone_device_resume()` without ensuring the old work had fully stopped, so `thermal_zone_device_unregister()` could miss a still-running work item and free the `thermal_zone_device` while it was still executing.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `cancel_delayed_work(&tz->poll_queue)` from `thermal_zone_pm_complete()`, adds a `tz->state & TZ_STATE_FLAG_EXIT` guard in `thermal_zone_device_resume()` to avoid re-arming work during teardown, and switches thermal events to a dedicated `thermal_wq` with `flush_workqueue(thermal_wq)` in `thermal_pm_notify()` because the old `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` path in `thermal_zone_device_unregister()` could miss already-running work after `INIT_DELAYED_WORK()`/`mod_delayed_work()` reinitialized `tz->poll_queue`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a read-only-after-init thermal workqueue pointer for use by the thermal subsystem.
intent_record.what: A new static pointer variable `thermal_wq` of type `struct workqueue_struct *` was added and marked with `__ro_after_init`.
intent_record.how: This introduces storage for a thermal subsystem workqueue that is intended to be initialized during early setup and then made read-only afterward, preventing later modification of the pointer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch thermal zone polling to the dedicated thermal workqueue to ensure it runs on the intended worker context.
intent_record.what: The call to mod_delayed_work() in thermal_zone_device_set_polling() was changed to use thermal_wq instead of system_freezable_power_efficient_wq while keeping the same delayed work item and delay calculation.
intent_record.how: At runtime, polling work for thermal zones will now be queued on the thermal-specific workqueue rather than the generic freezable power-efficient workqueue, changing which worker context executes the polling and how it is scheduled relative to other thermal tasks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip thermal zone resume handling when the zone is exiting to avoid operating on a device that is being removed.
intent_record.what: In `thermal_zone_device_resume(struct work_struct *work)`, a new comment and early return were added immediately after `guard(thermal_zone)(tz);`: if `tz->state & TZ_STATE_FLAG_EXIT` is true, the function returns before clearing `TZ_STATE_FLAG_SUSPENDED | TZ_STATE_FLAG_RESUMING` and before calling `thermal_debug_tz_resume(tz)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the resume work now does nothing for thermal zones that are already marked as exiting, preventing resume-time state updates and debug/resume handling on a device that is going away.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending thermal zone polling work during suspend preparation to prevent it from running after suspension begins.
intent_record.what: In `thermal_zone_pm_prepare(struct thermal_zone_device *tz)`, after setting `TZ_STATE_FLAG_SUSPENDED` on `tz->state`, the code now adds a call to `cancel_delayed_work(&tz->poll_queue);` with a new comment stating that this prevents new work from reaching the workqueue subsequently.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this stops any pending delayed thermal polling work associated with the thermal zone from being queued or executed after the zone has been marked suspended, reducing the chance of thermal polling activity continuing during suspend preparation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove delayed-work cancellation from thermal zone PM completion so polling is no longer stopped there.
intent_record.what: The call to `cancel_delayed_work(&tz->poll_queue);` was removed from `thermal_zone_pm_complete(struct thermal_zone_device *tz)`, while the subsequent `reinit_completion(&tz->resume);` and `tz->state |= TZ_STATE_FLAG_RESUMING;` lines remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the thermal zone resume-completion path no longer explicitly cancels the pending polling delayed work. This means an already scheduled poll work item may continue to exist or run instead of being forcefully canceled at this point in the PM flow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Queue thermal zone resume work on thermal_wq instead of the generic power-efficient workqueue.
intent_record.what: In thermal_zone_pm_complete(), the delayed work item tz->poll_queue is now queued on thermal_wq instead of system_freezable_power_efficient_wq, while keeping the zero-delay mod_delayed_work() call unchanged.
intent_record.how: This changes which workqueue executes the thermal zone resume work after power-management completion, causing it to run on the thermal subsystem's dedicated workqueue rather than the generic system freezable power-efficient queue.

intent_record.intent_summary: Flush pending thermal work during suspend and restore preparation to prevent leftover work from interfering with later power-management flow.
intent_record.what: In the PM_SUSPEND_PREPARE and PM_RESTORE_PREPARE notifier cases, the code now calls flush_workqueue(thermal_wq) immediately after thermal_pm_notify_prepare(), along with a new comment explaining that leftover thermal work items should be allowed to finish.
intent_record.how: When suspend or hibernation preparation begins, any pending thermal work queued on thermal_wq is forced to run to completion before the system proceeds. This prevents stale thermal work from remaining queued and interfering with later suspend/restore handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add initialization and cleanup for the thermal_events workqueue in thermal_init(), with proper error handling on allocation or setup failure.
intent_record.what: In thermal_init(), a new workqueue named "thermal_events" is allocated with alloc_workqueue() using WQ_FREEZABLE | WQ_POWER_EFFICIENT | WQ_PERCPU before thermal_register_governors() is called. If workqueue allocation fails, the code now sets result to -ENOMEM and jumps to unregister_netlink. The error path after thermal_register_governors() failure now jumps to destroy_workqueue instead of unregister_netlink.
intent_record.how: This creates a dedicated workqueue for thermal event processing during initialization, allowing thermal work to be queued and processed on a per-CPU, power-efficient, freezer-aware worker pool. It also ensures that if later initialization fails, the newly created workqueue is properly torn down, preventing resource leaks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing error-path cleanup to destroy the thermal workqueue during initialization failure.
intent_record.what: A new label `destroy_workqueue:` was added in `thermal_init()` between the existing `unregister_governors:` and `unregister_netlink:` error-handling paths, and it calls `destroy_workqueue(thermal_wq);`.
intent_record.how: If initialization fails after the thermal workqueue has been created, the cleanup path now explicitly destroys that workqueue before continuing to the netlink teardown, preventing the workqueue from being left allocated on error.

grouping_result.intent: Add a read-only-after-init thermal workqueue pointer for use by the thermal subsystem.
Queue thermal zone resume work on thermal_wq instead of the generic power-efficient workqueue.
Skip thermal zone resume handling when the zone is exiting to avoid operating on a device that is being removed.
Flush pending thermal work during suspend and restore preparation to prevent leftover work from interfering with later power-management flow.
Remove delayed-work cancellation from thermal zone PM completion so polling is no longer stopped there.
Add missing error-path cleanup to destroy the thermal workqueue during initialization failure.

consistency_review.core_intent: Update thermal zone work scheduling to use the dedicated thermal workqueue rather than the generic power-efficient workqueue.
Prevent pending thermal management work from running across suspend/restore transitions by canceling or flushing it during power-management preparation.
Add proper initialization and failure-path cleanup for the thermal workqueue during thermal subsystem setup.

relevance_review.reason: The change adds a read-only-after-init thermal workqueue pointer, which is unrelated to the race/use-after-free caused by reinitializing and reusing tz->poll_queue without waiting for prior work to stop.

The changes only move thermal zone work onto a dedicated workqueue. The root cause is a race from reusing/reinitializing tz->poll_queue without waiting for prior work to fully stop, which can let unregister free the device while work is still running. This group does not address that lifecycle/race condition.

The fix targets thermal zone resume handling during device removal, which is directly related to the race where delayed work could still be running while the thermal_zone_device is being unregistered and freed.

The changes directly target the thermal polling work lifecycle around suspend/restore by canceling/flushing pending work, which addresses the same class of bug as the root cause: reused delayed work that could still be running when the thermal zone is later unregistered and freed.

The root cause involves unsafe reuse/reinitialization of tz->poll_queue delayed work while it may still be running. Removing delayed-work cancellation from thermal_zone_pm_complete() directly changes the work lifecycle in this area and is related to the same polling/workqueue handling bug.

The changes are about initializing and cleaning up the thermal_events workqueue during thermal subsystem setup and handling init failures. They do not address the root cause involving reuse/reinitialization of tz->poll_queue delayed work during suspend/resume and the race with thermal_zone_device_unregister().

candidates.rationale: This is the work-cancelation point that was removed from thermal zone PM completion. The root cause says the delayed work was reused and reinitialized without ensuring the old work had fully stopped, allowing unregister to miss still-running work and free the device while it was executing.

This suspend-preparation path marks the zone suspended without itself guaranteeing the polling work is stopped first. In the vulnerable flow, suspend/resume state transitions could happen while delayed work remained active.

This is the PM-preparation entry that drives the suspend/restore handling. If the preparation path does not fully cancel or flush pending delayed work, the thermal zone can still have a running poll item across power-management transitions.
Clearing the suspended/resuming flags during resume without first ensuring the delayed polling work is no longer running contributes to reinitializing the zone while work may still be active.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the direct cancellation point for the thermal zone polling delayed work. The root cause is that the work could be reused/reinitialized and still be running when unregister occurs; removing or weakening this cancellation lets the old work persist and race with device teardown.

Clearing the suspended/resuming flags here allows resume handling to proceed without first ensuring the polling work is fully stopped, contributing to reinitialization of the thermal zone while delayed work may still be active.

This suspend-state transition occurs without by itself guaranteeing that the delayed polling work has fully stopped. In the vulnerable flow, the zone can enter suspend/resume transitions while work remains active, enabling the unregister race.

This PM-preparation entry drives suspend/restore handling for thermal zones. If the associated path does not fully flush or cancel the delayed polling work, the poll item can survive across power-management transitions and later race with unregister.
